message: Advent begins today. St. Ambrose wrote this hymn for his people in Milan sixteen centuries ago: all eight of his stanzas, in Latin, with English on screen. Veni, redemptor gentium. 🕯

Advent begins today. St. Ambrose of Milan wrote this hymn for his people sixteen centuries ago. Here is the stanza that gives it its name, sung in Latin with J. M. Neale's English. The whole hymn is on YouTube: @AllHolySaints, link in bio.

Veni, redemptor gentium. 🕯

Words: St. Ambrose of Milan (c. 339–397). Music and production: All Saints, created with AI assistance (Suno); icon AI-generated in the Byzantine style.

Christmas Eve. Fifteen centuries ago St. Romanos the Melodist sang these lines in Constantinople, and the Byzantine churches still sing them every Christmas: "Today the Virgin gives birth to the One beyond all being." Sung in Greek, with English on screen. 🕯

Christmas Eve. St. Romanos the Melodist wrote this hymn in Constantinople fifteen centuries ago, and the Byzantine churches still sing it every Christmas. Here are its closing lines, sung in Greek: for our sake is born a little Child, God before the ages. The whole hymn is on YouTube: @AllHolySaints, link in bio.

The Virgin today. 🕯

Words: St. Romanos the Melodist (c. 490–556). Music and production: All Saints, created with AI assistance (Suno); icon AI-generated in the Byzantine style.
